thread.title: Tech Today: Broadcompalooza, Lumentum for Oclaro, a Micron Breakout?

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Tech Today: Broadcompalooza, Lumentum for Oclaro, a Micron Breakout?
text:
Fiber optics consolidates, as Lumentum to buy Oclaro / CREDIT: Tiernan Ray for Barron's Here are some things going on today in your world of tech:
Fiber optic consolidation
The long-awaited consolidation in fiber-optic components appears to be getting underway. Lumentum Holdings ( LITE ) this morning said it will purchase Oclaro ( OCLR ) for $9.99 per share in cash and stock, including $5.60 a share and 0.0636 of a share of Lumentum for each Oclaro share.
Seems consolidation is something everyone likes : Oclaro stock is up $2.15, or 27%, at $10. Lumentum is up $5.38, or 8%, at $74.35. Finisar ( FNSR ), Lumentum’s biggest competitor, is up 91 cents, or 5%, a reprieve from a rough week of earnings news and downgrades last week.
Lumentum CEO Alan Lowe said Oclaro "brings its leading Indium Phosphide laser and Photonic Integrated Circuit and coherent component and module capabilities to Lumentum,” extending the company’ portfolio and “broadening our revenue mix."
Lumentum is holding a conference call this morning, and it issued a deck of slides on the deal .
As the Broadcom turns
It’s a vigorous morning in the ongoing drama between Broadcom ( AVGO ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ). Broadcom shares are up $7.09, or 3%, at $260.87, following a The Wall Street Journal report Friday that Intel ( INTC ) is closely watching Broadcom’s hostile bid for Qualcomm, and hoping Broadcom fails, so that Intel can buy Broadcom.
That was followed by Broadcom this morning saying its redomiciliation to the U.S. is expected to be completed by April 3rd.
But CNBC ’s David Faber related on air a short while ago that he has seen a copy of a letter sent to Broadcom and Qualcomm yesterday by the U.S. Treasury Department's CFIUS panel investigating the deal, stating that Broadcom violated on three counts the interim order that CFIUS issued a week ago and that CFIUS is angry with Broadcom. Broadcom is meeting with CFIUS today, reported Faber.
Debating the the Intel rumor, Stacy Rasgon of Bernstein writes he would ordinarily have “simply laughed this off,” though he “adds “we suppose we could develop some sort of strategic rationale.”
But RBC Capital ’s Amit Daryanani is more upbeat, writing that “We think AVGO (assuming a reasonable valuation is paid) would be an attractive acquisition for INTC. Our analysis shows the deal would be 85c-90c/20%+ accretive and would provide."
CNBC’s Faber relates that he’s heard Intel had hired bankers to mull a potential deal, but that “it seems unlikely right now,” meaning a deal.
Micron surges
Shares of DRAM and NAND memory chip maker Micron Technology ( MU ) are up $4.09, or almost 8%, at $58.68, after Instinet ’s Romit Shah this morning reiterated a Buy rating on the stock, and raised his price target to $100 from $55, writing that “after consolidating over the last 3-4 months,” the stock is "in the early stages of another major breakout .”
Also bullish this morning is Evercore ISI ’s C J Muse , who reiterates a Buy rating, and hikes his target to $80 from $60, writing that the "stock chart is scary” is "the first thing we hear from potential new investors (+500%+ over the last 2yrs)."
"But that’s what happens when the DRAM industry consolidates to 3, all players act rational, memory becomes increasingly critical in the world of compute, and rising complexity limits the magnitude of new supply,” writes Muse.
"So is the memory market different this time? Absolutely!"
Micron is to report earnings March 22nd, a week from Thursday.
Microsoft’s tone
Shares of Microsoft ( MSFT ) are down 7 cents at $96.47, despite an upbeat note from Deutsche Bank ’s Karl Keirstead this morning reiterated a Buy rating on the shares, and raised his price target to $120 from $115, following an investor meeting with the company in Seattle, in which the “tone” improved about the Office, Server, and Azure businesses, according to a write-up from TheFlyontheWall .
Among other software notes today, Kirk Materne of Evercore raises his rating on SAP ( SAP ) to Outperform from “In Line,” while cutting Hubspot ( HUBS ) to In Line from Outperform.
Shares of SAP are down 34 cents at $108.78 while Hubspot is down $2.70, or 2%, at $117.80.
And shares of Red Hat ( RHT ) are down $1.51, or 1%, at $153.97, after Mizuho ’s Abhey Lamba cut his rating on the stock this morning to Neutral from Buy, even as he raised his price target to $60 from $40.
"We think fundamentals are strong with enterprise spending trends remain buoyant in the current environment,” writes Lamba. “However, we think the stock fully reflects this at the current valuation."
Dropbox updates IPO plans
Dropbox , which filed on February 23rd an S1 prospectus with the Securities & Exchange Commission to go public, this morning offered an amended version , stating it expects to sell 26.8 million shares in the offering, in a price up to $18 per share.
In addition, the company says that certain selling stockholders will dispose of 9.18 million shares.
Goldman Sachs is lead underwriter of the deal.
Spielberg directs Nvidia, AMD
Jefferies & Co. analyst Mark Lipacis this morning writes that “Ready Player One,” the forthcoming film from Steven Spielberg , may be a “catalyst” for Nvidia ( NVDA ) and Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ). “The movie will drive sales of VR headsets that require high-performance GPUs” from both companies, he writes.
Nvidia shares are up $7.15, or 3%, at $252.48, and AMD shares are up 10 cents, or 0.9%, at $11.80.
The wait for Android 3-D sensing
You may not be getting that “ 3-D sensing ” capability in your Android -based phone just yet. DigiTimes ’s Cage Chao and Steve Shen on Friday reportedt that makers of phones are “still reluctant to adopt 3D sensing technology for their new models to be launched in 2018 due to the persistent high prices of 3D sensing modules, citing Taiwanese chip-industry sources.
Apple ( AAPL ) uses 3-D sensing in the front-facing camera of the iPhone X to produce the “ Face ID ” capability. It has been expected it would rapidly spread to Android phones. The authors write that supply of some parts is constrained, keeping prices of models high. They cite prices of $30 to $50.
